enquiry: We handle a petroleum stream and currently send samples to a laboratory for water determination. We want to investigate a fiber based measurement closer to the process so that changes can be noticed sooner. The analyzer would be outside the process area. Before selecting equipment, we need to know what to clarify and what a first comparison experiment should establish.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when water changes are only known from laboratory results, and what decision should real-time data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Defines the value of earlier detection and the decision the in-line signal must support.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Earlier detection is the goal; the decision and its urgency are unknown until clarified.

clarification_questions.question: What is the water level of interest in the petroleum stream, expressed in ppm or %, and over what range does it vary?
clarification_questions.why: The concentration level decides whether the method must be sensitive to trace water or to bulk water.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether it is ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: Is the stream a clear liquid, turbid, or opaque, and does it contain a separate water phase, emulsion or solids?
clarification_questions.why: Optical appearance and phase state decide the probe geometry and the suitable spectral range.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical form unknown; a lab screening on representative samples establishes it before probe choice.

clarification_questions.question: What are the process temperature, pressure, and fouling or cleaning conditions at the sampling point, and how much does the stream composition vary?
clarification_questions.why: These conditions affect probe survival, fouling and calibration robustness.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Conditions unknown; the in-line trial must document them before scale-up.

clarification_questions.question: Where exactly would the probe be installed, what is the distance from the measuring point to the analyzer outside the process area, and are any fibers already installed?
clarification_questions.why: Distance and existing fibers determine which wavelengths can reach the analyzer and whether a remote setup is feasible.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Distance and fiber availability unknown; the choice of fiber type and range is deferred.

clarification_questions.question: Which laboratory method is used for water determination today, what is its accuracy, and how often are samples taken?
clarification_questions.why: The reference method and its accuracy define the benchmark for the first comparison experiment.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and accuracy unknown; the comparison design cannot be fixed until they are known.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the fiber-based measurement?
clarification_questions.why: These requirements select the simplest method that meets the need and set the scope of the trial.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; the simplest candidate method is assessed first.

items.text: ATR probe for MIR; transmission or transflection probe for NIR; final geometry follows the stream's optics.
Closer to the process than lab sampling; exact point unknown.
Link unknown. Silica fibers transmit 350-2400 nm; CIR 1.1-6.5 um; PIR 3-17 um. Which suits MIR coverage is an inference; no link lengths given.

No fiber link stated. Rule check: MIR full range: no single fiber; partial: Chalcogenide As-S IR fiber (CIR), Polycrystalline silver halide IR fiber (PIR), Hollow glass waveguide (HWG), Indium fluoride fiber, Zirconium fluoride fiber; NIR full range: Indium fluoride fiber, Zirconium fluoride fiber; partial: UV-Vis silica fiber (standard or Al/Cu-coated), Vis-NIR silica fiber (standard or Al/Cu-coated), Chalcogenide As-S IR fiber (CIR), Hollow glass waveguide (HWG).

flags_before_revision.detail: different_context: The S02 p.13 slide is an AFS application note about ATR probes with ZrO2/diamond tips in petroleum; it does not state the probe is MIR-ATR or that it is the first candidate for this stream. The claim transfers the example's suitability without support for this specific project. Fix: Say that the AFS water-in-petroleum slide shows an ATR probe example for oil with water, which is a reasonable starting point to test, not a validated choice for this stream.

not_supported: The cited pages support the 1-6 um ATR depth and CIR/PIR fiber needs only partly; the claim that contact and fouling matter is not stated on the cited table rows or the notes, which only give qualitative ratings. Fix: Limit the caveat to the ATR depth of about 1-6 um from the table and state contact and fouling as a general practical consideration not taken from these pages.

overstated: S01 p.5 says NIR is ideal for online applications and remote measurements via fiber probes; it does not say NIR is simpler or cheaper than the alternatives for this link. Fix: Say NIR is described as suited to online and remote fiber measurement, and cost or simplicity comparison requires further evidence.

not_supported: The fiber-range rule check lists MIR and NIR coverage categories that are not stated on S02 p.6, which only gives transmission ranges per fiber type; the full/partial classifications are inferences. Fix: Restate only the wavelength ranges shown on S02 p.6 and mark the full/partial classification as an inference.

not_supported: S01 p.10 discusses ATR fiber probes and NIR online analysis but does not state that a change in petroleum composition or matrix invalidates a calibration. Fix: Attribute the calibration risk to general chemometric practice, or cite a page that discusses calibration model validity.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
